keyTakeaways: A readable Word export is a handoff document, not certification that a translation, rights clearance, or submission package is complete.
SurtitleLive's current Word export produces one selected language in colon or centred-character layout, with stage-direction and missing-translation choices.
Review structure before translation, then review the target language both line by line and scene by scene.
Follow the recipient's requirements and add credits, version status, rights information, contacts, and supporting material where required.

faq.question: Can SurtitleLive export a translated play as a Word document?
faq.answer: Yes. The Editor exports one selected source or translated language as a DOCX in colon or centred-character layout.

faq.question: Does the Word export create a bilingual parallel script?
faq.answer: No. Provide separate source and target exports or assemble and review a bilingual document outside the current Word-export flow.

faq.question: What is the safest missing-translation setting for a submission copy?
faq.answer: Stopping the export until missing target-language lines are resolved is generally the clearest external-submission default.

faq.question: Can the exported script be projected as live surtitles?
faq.answer: Not unchanged. Live audience text needs separate segmentation, cueing, display decisions, and rehearsal.

glossary.definition: A script prepared for a recipient to assess the work, distinct from a rehearsal or performance document.
The chosen behaviour when a target-language line is absent: stop, use source text, leave blank, or mark the gap.
A Word script layout in which a speaker label and colon precede the dialogue.
A Word script layout in which the character name appears centred on a separate line.
A truthful description of a document's purpose and review state, such as translator-reviewed reading copy.
